note: The three branch-merge arities that had only a Script-VM unit test behind them: k=2 symmetric (`bothArms`), k=3 (`three`) and merged-at-the-outer-level nesting (`nested`). Plan Phase D1 asks for the same real-secp256k1 / real-BIP-143 continuation proof `branch-merged-locals` gets for the asymmetric k=2 case. Every accept pins expectedState, so a merge that resurrects a dead pre-branch binding fails on the VALUE even when the spend would still be accepted. Constructor state is (a,b,c) = (0,0,9); `c` is the untouched control field — a merge that shifts a stack slot corrupts it.

spends.note: k=2 symmetric, then-arm: na=x+1=11, nb=x+2=12, c untouched
k=2 symmetric, else-arm: na=x+3=13, nb=x+4=14, c untouched
k=3, then-arm: 21, 22, 23 — all three merged locals reach the continuation
nested: outer taken, inner then-arm rebinds na only — nb must survive from before the OUTER if
nested: outer taken, inner else-arm rebinds nb only — na must survive
nested: outer NOT taken (no else) — the implicit fallthrough arm rebinds neither local, so both originals must reach the continuation
tampered continuation output — the k=3 merged result block must be committed to by hashOutputs
